newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-NINE-MAN TENERIFE HANG ON TO BEAT SCHALKE 1-0.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-NINE-MAN TENERIFE HANG ON TO BEAT SCHALKE 1-0.

text.p: Spain's Tenerife hung on for a 1-0 win over Schalke despite conceding a penalty and being reduced to nine men in an exciting UEFA Cup semifinal first leg match on Tuesday.
Tenerife went ahead through a fifth-minute penalty but lost their way when Angel Vivar Dorado was sent off early in the second half.
They then survived a penalty miss after goalkeeper Marcelo Ojeda was dismissed 15 minutes from the end.
The Spaniards controlled the opening phase of the match and were rewarded quickly when Juanele Castanos broke down the right and was brought down in the area by Schalke captain Olaf Thon.
Felipe Minambres had no problem in sending keeper Jens Lehmann the wrong way from the spot.
With midfielder Slavisa Jokanovica feeling the effects of a knee injury, Juanele, Felipe and Antonio Pinilla took control as Schalke struggled to find their feet.
Midway through the first half Pinilla and Juanele broke free together and were bearing down on goal but got tangled up in one another and wasted a clear chance to score.

Shortly afterwards it was Schalke's turn to fall victims to misunderstanding as Ingo Anderbruegge saw his follow up shot blocked by a team mate after Tenerife keeper Marcelo Ojeda parried his initial effort.
Andreas Mueller and Jiri Nemec also went close as Schalke turned up the pressure towards the interval.

The Germans started strongly after the break, but it was Tenerife's Felipe who came closest to scoring in the early minutes, curling wide a shot after the Spaniards regained the ball after a mistake by Thon.
But ten minutes into the second half the game changed shape radically when Angel Vivar Dorado was sent off for elbowing Radoslav Latal in retaliation for a heavy challenge.
From then on Tenerife lived dangerously as Schalke's Marc Wilmots hit the bar with a header and Ingo Anderbruegge forced two fine saves out of Ojeda.
Often the Spaniards were their own worse enemies and it was a mistake in midfield that let Wilmots slice through the home defence in the 75th minute.
Ojeda's last-ditch challenge earned him a red card and his place was taken by substitute goalkeeper Bengt Andersson.
The Swede was saved the indignity of picking the ball out of the net with his first touch because Johan de Kock blast the penalty wide.

But Andersson was called on to make a series of saves in a frantic last 15 minutes as Schalke tried to squeeze the most out of their two-man advantage by bringing on strikers Tom Dooley and David Wagner.
Compensation for Schalke, who deserved at least a draw, may come in the second leg.

Schalke will play the game without suspended Andreas Mueller but Tenerife will be without Ojeda, Vivar Dorado and Antonio Robaiana, who was sent off in their last tie. Also missing will be Juanele, who spoiled a fine performance with a booking late in the game.
